originality.rationale: Rains Theorem 3.4 gives the fundamental-character trace-moment count (including its exceptional dimension-two value), not the sixth moment of every rectangular quaternionic coefficient nor the singular-value extrema. Collins–Śniady supplies general symplectic integration machinery, which can implicitly recover moment coefficients but does not state the positive spectral deficits, equality geometry, or optimal Euclidean distortion. Tropp compares real Stiefel matrices to Gaussian matrices, not exact quaternionic sixth norms. The closest accessible research ledger claims address real orthogonal Haar matrices or distinct real-valued random models; published-finding corpus semantic searches found no theorem with the same quaternionic object, moment, full coefficient domain and sharp equality conclusions. Residual bibliographic risk persists.
residual_risks: A specialized indexed-under-different-terminology symplectic trace-moment/spectral inequality may imply the optimized formula without using these expressions.

value.rationale: A complete two-parameter family of real L6 normed spaces is characterized exactly, not just a single trace-moment example. The result provides sharp ratio endpoints, rigidity of rank-one and equal singular-value geometries, quantitative two-sided spectral stability and exact Banach–Mazur distortion, while detecting the structural symplectic n=2 trace defect. These are intrinsic to a natural Haar Stiefel observable and enable precise norm comparisons.
